It is explained in all the books and especially in his own book, Part II, section 7: that this Tzaddik who learns with the dwellers above and the dwellers below (without which he cannot be called a Tzaddik if he is unable to do this — was such a revelation heard or seen like it?) — even when he passes on, he has not entirely passed on. For he knows well — for the primary thing is "and she desires praise from those who dwell in the dust" etc. See there. And he concluded there — "and this is the aspect of the burial of Moshe." And the rabbi of our community, the wondrous Gaon of blessed memory, explained that this alludes that even when this Tzaddik passes on — his holy grave will accomplish all the many actions mentioned in that Torah teaching. And therefore there was a testament from him that one travel to his holy grave and say there the ten known Psalms that he revealed for the rectification of the covenant, may the Merciful One protect us — which is the root of all sins, flaws, and bad character traits — as is known from the holy Zohar and from all the books of truth and in particular from his holy book.

For know that there will be no more leaders of households (see in the Torah "Bereishis" in section 67 Part II of his book and you will understand this) until the coming of Moshiach our righteousness. Therefore he placed his power in his book and promised to help whoever will come to his grave until the end. And about this he left his testament in these words: "Nor ir zalt zech haltin in eynem un mekablin dein min dein" [Only hold yourselves together and receive this from one another].

For the power and counsels he placed in his book are hidden and deep — especially those holy counsels needed now that were not yet needed then — therefore they were not seen in his holy book (just as the holy Zohar was physically hidden — so here spiritually) — until the final generation that needs them for its healing arrives — and will search at his holy grave and in his books until they are found — as it is written: "Deep waters is counsel in a man's heart — and a man of understanding will draw it out" [Mishlei 20:5]. For the deep counsels will only be revealed through a cry from the depth of the heart — as it is written: "From the depths I called to You" — "their heart cried out to Hashem."

Therefore certainly you have done well to arouse in your thoughts in Eider HaYakar [your book] — but this is only appropriate with the joining and magnification of the power of analytical study in this precious and wondrous legacy — and in the books of his holy disciple Reb Noson of blessed memory.

Praise to G-d — for Yisrael is not widowed of its G-d — for Hashem saw our affliction and sent the remedy before the blow. For these three years the hearts of our dear followers have been aroused to gather a number of young scholars to the yeshiva in the great study house called by his name — here in Uman, the place of his holy burial, newly built. And until now it was open only from Rosh HaShanah to Rosh HaShanah — at the time of the gathering of all our dear followers at his holy grave. And now the hearts of our dear followers have been aroused — since they saw the greatness of the darkness of the world and the greatness of the true effect of the holy counsels flowing from his holy book — and only they can save in these end of days. And there was divine providence from Him and from this Tzaddik who still stands and prays for us — for the man will not rest until the matter is completed today. And Hashem has prepared people like arrows in the hand of a warrior — thus are the children of one's youth. They will not be shamed when they speak with enemies in the gate. And I the small one am one of them. And may Hashem help that there be no impediment regarding livelihood.

And praise to G-d — they study Talmud and Poskim — and the primary fixed period between Minchah and Maariv is two hours of study of faith — as explained in Torah section 5 above: that one must establish a regular session for the study of faith — as it is written: "so that you may learn to fear" — and especially in the words of his faithful disciple through whom he intended the understanding of his master's words in the explanation of his holy words — Reb Noson of blessed memory.

And praise to G-d — we have a true preacher who brings to light the hidden things of his book — and he is his holy grandson [Reb Shimshon Barsky, of blessed memory]. And he prevails with his song to bring this learning down to all levels. And he is truly G-d-fearing and complete in true faith and faith in the wise — and draws himself toward all the 48 things through which Torah is acquired. And humble and lowly in truth without any name as our Rabbainu taught us. Therefore among the famous ones — their sons conduct themselves after them even when they do not know why. But here it does not go by inheritance — only previously there was his holy disciple and the like — and now that one is found ready for this from those who come from his loins — how good and how pleasant. But without public fanfare — only he searches for the true counsel to save his soul from the flood of many waters — for he saw that the evil was coming to him — that he was nearly caught in this evil. And through this others are also saved. And constantly people come and are added — new souls to hear this learning and to taste its taste. And they say "Aha — I have seen light!" And from time to time he rouses to speak of the spirit of the time that rumbles now — a shadow of death without order — the likes of which our fathers never imagined. And he seeks to examine according to these teachings how they contradict truth and faith — and also contradict simple upright reason — and how their hearts became twisted and their minds and knowledge became corrupted — so they cannot see what is developing.

But every city stands on its hill — while the city of G-d is lowered down to the nethermost pit. For due to the concealment that intensified from then upon this path — of which the pen and paper do not agree to speak now — therefore even now it is still in concealment. And we know the primary truth because the adversary saw that through this path Yisrael would return to her beloved — therefore he counseled to conceal the light. But the counsel of Hashem stands forever — "and You are exalted forever Hashem" — and Rashi explained: "forever Your hand is on top." And Rabbainu said before his passing: "Have I not completed? I have completed and I will complete! Mein feyerl vet shoyn tluyen biz Moshiach vet kumen [My little fire will already burn until Moshiach comes]." And Rabbainu said: "I have already prepared everything for Moshiach our righteousness — and with these paths he will complete it!" But we must prepare ourselves for this — so that at any rate we understand his language and he can engage — as it is written in Michah 2:13: "The one who breaks through goes up before them — they break through and pass through the gate and go out through it" — see in Metzudas Dovid there and understand carefully.

Therefore may his honor fulfill the teaching of our Sages: "Happy is the generation when the great listen to the small." And as we saw in your books Eider HaYakar — that Hashem awakened your good spirit to look at the affliction of Yisrael and to rouse the heart of the wise of Yisrael to strive for their remedy. The truth I will acknowledge and not be ashamed — that I did not grasp all his thoughts to their depth — because of the difficult and foreign words found in it — in its being clothed in a foreign garment so that it would be accepted in all eyes. And he did good for his people — as Rabbainu said on the verse: "He changes his appearance and they sent him away" — see there in section 60. And "the words of the mouth of a wise man are grace." But this seems to me — that had you known the goodness of these books and their conversation — then you would not have had to change your garment so much. For those who speak in this language are few — and there is serious doubt whether they will incline their hearts through this toward the good and straight path. But the majority of our people need simple Judaic speech — then perhaps all of this may work in their hearts to save them from the chaos and confusion and darkness and abyss that has developed in these end of days. For they are tzippurey melichei [salted/mixed birds — meaning they lean both ways] as Rabbainu called them in Part II section 4 — see there. And even though these are simple things — yet their foundations are in the mountains of holiness — from a holy source their quarry — from a holy place they walk. For this simplicity is bounded overall by wisdom — for the primary wisdom is wholeness and simplicity (as Rabbainu said in the Sipuray Ma'asiyos in the story of the Wise Man and the Simple Man — see there). Only one must prepare a vessel to receive this wisdom within — and the vessel is faith. As Reb Noson said on the teaching of the Tikkunim on the verse: "With this shall Aharon enter the sanctuary" — "come and see — no person realizes his desire from Hashem except through this..." — this is what is written: "This I will return to my heart — therefore I will hope" — "with this I trust". And the prophet — when he saw Yisrael in exile — saw no rest for them except through this — "and the redemption of Yisrael will come only through this." See there at wondrous length as he expands on the matter of "this" — and Reb Noson explained that "this" is Malchus — as written in the Tikkunay HaZohar — and Malchus is the attribute of the holy faith. And this is what is written there: "no prophet or seer or wise person has permission to enter except through her" — for she is the vessel for all true knowledge.

Therefore the primary thing is to bring into Yisrael the attribute of holy faith in all its aspects — namely faith in the Creator, and faith in true wise ones. For beyond the greatness of their understanding and counsel that they bring into us — the greatness of their power surpasses everything. For the primary counsel of all counsels is the counsel of Hashem — that is, a counsel within which Hashem is clothed — it will stand. Therefore the power of the Tzaddikim is needed — for all their words and deeds are filled with holy spirit in which the spirit of Hashem spoke through them and His word is on their tongue. For through the greatness of their power and their quality as a segulah — and also the quality of studying their words as a segulah — they subdue the power of the evil venom that is clothed within them through their evil deeds — as it is written: "for it is only your iniquities that have been separating between Me and you" — that is, between the attainment of truth.

And therefore "they are wise to do evil and how to do good they do not know" — and Rabbainu explained: for through their evil deeds their intellect is corrupted and darkened — to the point where they cannot use their intellect at all for good — only for evil. And great powers are needed for their healing — so that there not be the aspect that Rabbainu wrote — these are his words: "And of these Torah scholars it is said: 'Is it too small a thing for you to weary men — that you weary also my G-d' — meaning they weary the people who come to hear their homilies and Torah. And people think that through them they will come to some benefit — namely to know how to serve Hashem — and these people attain no benefit at all. For the Torah of these Torah scholars has no power to guide a person in the good path — for from evil there comes no good. And furthermore — 'they weary also G-d' — as if the Holy One blessed be He is weary of helping those who serve Him. It follows that through this these people fall into great heresy — and think, G-d forbid, that G-d neither sees nor understands the deeds of human beings — and through this they do not honor those who fear Hashem." See there at length in his holy language in section 28.

But the true Tzaddikim are wondrous and exalted in their power — as Reb Noson wrote in his precious book Alim LiTerufah — these are his words: "And I know and believe in truth that our master, our teacher and Rabbainu, knows well — in generality and in particularity — all that has happened with all the souls in every generation from the day G-d created man on the earth until now — until the very final end. And he knows all the rectifications of each and every one — and all this knowledge is to him a small matter." See there in letter 256 at the length of his holy words... And how he can heal all the ailments of his people Yisrael — as it is written: "On the day Hashem binds the fracture of His people and heals the wound of His blow" — and about him is said the verse: "And you shall draw water with joy from the springs of salvation" — and its translation: "you shall receive new teaching from the chosen Tzaddikim."

For upon him is said what Rabbainu said in section 5, Part II: "The words of Hashem are pure words — silver refined in a crucible in the earth — purified seven times" [Tehillim 12:7] — meaning these pure words like purified silver that come from these minds that are included from the seven shepherds — as it is written: "Raise up for us a shepherd of seven" — meaning this shepherd who will be composed of all the seven shepherds — specifically he can heal all the souls included in the verse "seven times the righteous man falls and rises." And he heals them with seven answers to taste. See there carefully and you will see a new light — how sweet is the light. Would that you had tasted from the honeycomb — pleasant words sweet to the soul and healing to the bone. All these praises that you wrote in praise of the upright man — and all these actions for good that were effected through him in all the descriptions you described — whether in his character traits or in his ways of life — how many times would they be multiplied here! And furthermore there is here an additional advantage — that even after his holy passing his power will be magnified to refine the souls of those connected to him — to open the eyes in his holy books to direct his holy intention — to find all the remedies needed for his soul at all times.

For many times pass over a person individually and over the nation collectively — as it is written: "and the times that passed over him and over Yisrael." And with this Reb Noson explains the verse: "and from the children of Yissachar — those who know understanding of times to know what Yisrael should do" [Divrei HaYamim I 12:33]. For the great Tzaddik is called Yissachar — after the verse "Rachel weeps for her children." This alludes to the totality of Yisrael and also every individual soul — who is like Rachel silent before her shearers — for the kelipas and the nations shear and take from her her glory and her splendor in the physical and spiritual — "she refused to be comforted for her children" — meaning the primary offspring of Tzaddikim are commandments and good deeds. But by her even the good deeds are deficient — and she cannot be comforted through them — for there is no true Tzaddik — only through whose power all the deeds of all Yisrael can be completed.

And since the Tzaddikim have passed on — therefore the good deeds of all Yisrael are not complete — and they do not accomplish what they need and can accomplish through them. And when this distant individual, and the entire nation collectively, is aroused in the depth of its distance — and does not despair of itself because of its great distance in any way — and cries and calls out to Hashem always — this is the aspect of: "A voice is heard in Ramah — weeping and bitter crying" — as above. Even though she herself knows the greatness of her obligation — but even so — since she still strengthens herself to cry and weep to Hashem always — then the mercies of Hashem are roused and shine upon her illumination and encouragement from above — in the aspect of: "Thus says Hashem: 'Withhold your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears — for there is reward for your work and there is hope for your end.'"

And all this Hashem makes known to her only through the Tzaddik of the generation great in level exceedingly — who is in the aspect of Yissachar — who shines on each soul of Yisrael individually and collectively — and informs her that still "there is reward" — for no word and no cry is lost — even a cry from the nethermost pit is never lost forever. As Rabbainu said in Yiddish: "Gewald! Zait aich nit meyaesh!" [Gevald! Do not despair!] And he drew out the word "Gewald" greatly — to hint for always and for generations in general and individually — that they not despair of themselves in any way whatsoever — even if whatever happens upon them. And he hinted to us in his holy words that all his concern in coming to this world was only to raise and elevate and rectify all the fallen souls. And once he said about himself: "My hands are soiled with blood and birth-fluid and afterbirth in order to purify..."

Especially now in the heels of Moshiach's times — in the time of the spreading of the awesome darkness — doubled and redoubled — chaos and disorder — which even the earlier prophets saw and were astonished at how the holy children of Yisrael would be able to strengthen themselves in the faith of Hashem and in His pure fear within this darkness. And blessed be Hashem who sent the remedy before the blow — and sent us a savior and teacher — Nachal Novea Mekor Chochmah — who, he and his holy disciples, informed us of the abundance of His mercies and kindnesses beyond all searching.

And this is the explanation of "and from the children of Yissachar" — namely the disciples of this Tzaddik who is called Yissachar as above (for disciples are called sons) — they are "knowers of understanding of times." For in all the times that pass over every individual of Yisrael, and over the nation collectively — as it is written: "In Your hands are my times — save me from the hand of my enemies and those who pursue me." And this is the primary completeness of the great Tzaddik — as Yissachar — who teaches knowledge and Torah to Yisrael — who can illuminate for every individual of Yisrael that he can strengthen himself and remain standing in all the times and occasions that pass over them. And this is "to know what Yisrael should do." And this is the explanation of the teaching of our Sages: "Why was the Torah given to Yisrael? Because they are brazen." For it is impossible to be a true Yisraeli and serve Him as required and hold oneself in faith in Him in all times as above — except through great holy boldness and stubbornness — to stand against all the instigators and misleaders — against a crooked and twisted generation like this — as it is written: "Give strength to G-d... He gives strength and might to the people — blessed is G-d."

But they turn upright paths — for they use boldness and stubbornness for foreign things — for the pursuit of honor and domination. And they transgress the holy Mishnah: "Pray for the welfare of the government" — and the Midrash on the verse: "I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem" — three oaths the Holy One blessed be He made Yisrael swear in exile — and one of them: that they not rebel against the government. And if not — "I permit your flesh like the deer and the gazelles of the field." See there.

And how does one merit to turn the hearts of the children of Yisrael toward Him — to raise these fallen character traits to their root in holiness — to use these traits of "boldness and stubbornness" for the service of Hashem — to raise up the holy kingship from exile through the coming of Moshiach our righteousness. And Rabbainu said: "The primary weapon of Moshiach is prayer" — as it is written: "For not in my bow will I trust and my sword will not save me... for in G-d we boast" — and it is written: "and with my sword and my bow" — and Rashi explained: with my prayer and my entreaty.

And for prayer great boldness and stubbornness is required — as Rabbainu wrote in section 30 at its end: for it is impossible to stand and pray before Hashem except through boldness — for each one according to what his heart imagines of the greatness of the Creator — as written in the holy Zohar: "He is known in the gates through her husband — each one according to what his heart imagines." How is it possible for him to stand and pray before Him — and especially prayer which is wonders — namely the disruption of the natural order — where the natural order demands thus (in our matter — that every king is established in his kingdom and we want to enthrone the holy kingship which is lowly). And every star and constellation is fixed on its watch and its arrangement as the Creator arranged them. And he comes with his prayer and wants to disrupt the natural order and work wonders. Therefore at the time of prayer one must put aside shame — as it is written: "In You our fathers trusted... they trusted and were not ashamed." For through shame it is impossible to pray before Him — except through boldness.

And this is the aspect of: "You are the G-d who does wonders — You made known among the peoples Your strength." For Hashem works wonders through the prayers of Yisrael — which are through the aspect of boldness. Through this He makes known to the nations the holy boldness of Yisrael — as our Sages said: "These Torah scholars who are weak as women yet perform mighty deeds as men" — and this is only through holy powers which is the power of Hashem — not according to nature. As it is written: "The children of Efraim — armed bowmen — turned back in the day of battle" — meaning they went out before their time and trusted in their strength as is known. Due to the fact that the illumination of the approaching end had already begun to sparkle — and it reached even them. Only since they did not purify their vessels — therefore the impurity turned by their understanding into trust in their strength and the might of their hand. Therefore they fell like dung upon the face of the earth. And similarly now.

And it is also explained in the Yosefon that at the time of the destruction of the Second Temple it was thus — that the wicked ones trusted in their strength. And through this they had no mercy even on others — just as now — where it cannot be believed how great is the outrage and revolution that exists among us now — even between a man and his fellow: the robberies and murders that now specifically this new generation — educated in wisdoms, with Bildung and Eidlkeit [culture and refinement] — and where is their wisdom and refinement? Do they not know and understand and see that the fear of Hashem is wisdom and knowledge of the Holy Ones is understanding — and outside of this everything is vanity — as it is written: "Behold they do not know Hashem and what wisdom is theirs?" And as it is written: "Let not the wise man boast of his wisdom nor the mighty man of his might nor the rich man of his riches — but only with this... to understand and know Me" — meaning to use all these traits to understand and know Me — which is for prayer — as it is written: "Know the G-d of your father and serve Him" — what service of the heart — this is prayer.

For it is stated in the books — just as the work of the earth is called by the name "labor" more than any other craft — weaving, smelting, and calculating — for just as the slave who prepares everything at the command of his master who makes the machines — everything needed for his production: iron, coals, water, and all the implements — he will place and prepare in the place his master commanded him. Afterward his master comes and prepares the implement for his work with his great wisdom — knowing how to combine everything for his production. While the slave understands nothing of how his master formed such a wondrous machine. So too the working of the earth — for in truth the working is only the one who prepares for its actions — each thing in its place. But the very sprouting and growing and ripening — not only is it beyond his ability to accomplish any action in this — but he also does not understand in what way and how the seed can absorb, and how from one grain a hundred grains grow — for no living creature has yet understood the reason of nature. And from this we should understand the designation of prayer by the name "labor" — for also we do not understand in what way, and how actions are accomplished through our prayers. Only we are obligated to do this — like a slave to his master — without any asking of reasons.

And for this too great stubbornness is needed — as Rabbainu wrote in section 2 on the teaching of Rabbah bar bar Chanah: "And we saw that fish" — this is the aspect of the Tzaddik of the generation who is called "fish" (as stated in the Talmud and Midrash: just as the gathering of fish is their purification — so Tzaddikim). "Sand settled on it" — this is the aspect of prayers (as written: "And Moshe pleaded") that we pray beside him — regarding his having turned his back toward us in the aspect of the hiding of the face — that he return and shine his face toward us. "It was resting on it" — meaning: "And they brought the Tabernacle to Moshe" — for one must bring the Tabernacle to the Tzaddik of the generation (for every prayer is an aspect of a limb of the Shechinah — the aspect of the Tabernacle, the house that will be built speedily in our days — "Hashem who builds Jerusalem... through all the prayers of Yisrael"). For only he knows how to fit each limb to limb to make from it a complete stature (like the parable of the machine and the working of the earth we mentioned). "And we thought it was dry land" — meaning the prayers do not bear fruit, G-d forbid. But in truth this is not so — only "we went up on it" — namely the prayers ascend. "When it warmed, it overturned" — namely when His attribute of mercy is heated — He overturns from the back — the attribute of judgment — to the attribute of mercy.

It follows that great stubbornness is needed in prayer — so they do not think it is dry land, G-d forbid. And even if it appears no action is accomplished — wait and wait and multiply prayer — until the stature of the Shechinah is built through the true Tzaddik. Even so "had we not been close to the ship" — meaning for my sake will I do this — for safina [ship] is the aspect of kindness as our Sages said "most sailors are pious." Without His kindness we would drown, G-d forbid, in exile. It follows that even for prayer — only His kindness is needed. And all the more so that with physical hands nothing can be accomplished at all — for "the hands are the hands of Esav and the voice is the voice of Yaakov" — as stated in the Midrash: at the time when the voice of Yaakov — that is, prayer — is not operating — then the hands of Esav rule, G-d forbid. Such is a small taste of the paths of Rabbainu's ways.
And indeed in your book too you speak of this kind of thing. But would that this light had illuminated upon him — then with his power he would rise — who is like him as a teacher?

And we request of him that he write to us briefly — what is his intention in his book for practical application — whether his intention is the path of Zionism — of which we are not pleased — for this is also included in the aspect of "the hands are the hands of Esav." Or another intention. And perhaps there is a way to explain the foreign words found in his book — so that understanding be gained from it — and to teach those distant ones who need specifically this language — you may explain to our dear followers also in the Land of Yisrael in Tzfas and in Yerushalayim.

Even though they asked the young scholar Reb Yaakov Yosef who brought his book to us — whether there is a Gaon among us? — have I not already written to you the teaching of our Sages: "A handmaid at the sea saw what Yechezkel did not see." And understand this.
Thus speaks the lowly one who desires the truth —
Elyakim Getzil Leibavone
Be strong, be strong and let us strengthen ourselves!
Completed and finished — praise to G-d Creator of the world
